rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.e1: Attack: this position comes from a London. White has brought the bishop to f4 and the knight to f3, and Black has put the bishop on g7. Nobody has a check, a threat or a capture that wins material.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.e2: Before playing your own plan, ask: what does the opponent want to do? The knight on f6 wants to go to h5, to trade off the bishop on f4. The bishop on c8 wants to go to g4, to pin the knight on f3 against the queen.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l0: The pawn goes to h3: it takes g4 away from the black bishop and knight and opens h2 for the bishop on f4.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l1: Black castles to tuck the king away before going to h5 with the knight.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l2: White carries on with their plan: the bishop comes out, and castling is ready.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l3: The knight goes to h5 and attacks the bishop on f4.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l4: The bishop drops back to h2, the square the h3 pawn left free. There is no trade, and the bishop stays on the same diagonal.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.london.l5: The pawn move to h3 threatened nothing: it took away what the opponent wanted to do. This is called prophylaxis. In quiet positions like this one, ask what the opponent wants before playing your own plan.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.p: Find the move that stops Black's plan.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.certo: The pawn goes to b3 and closes the diagonal. The bishop has no way out: your king covers b1 and b3.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.revela: The pawn goes to b3 and closes the diagonal the bishop would use. Your king covers b1 and b3, and the bishop is trapped.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.b2b4.1: With this move, the bishop gets out along the diagonal: it passes b3 and goes to c4, back into play.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.b2b4.2: Back to the position: where does the bishop on a2 want to get out? Close that exit.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.h2h4.1: The pawn advances, but the move stops nothing: the bishop passes b3 and goes to d5, back into play.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.h2h4.2: Back to the position: where does the bishop on a2 want to get out? Close that exit.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.c3c4.1: The pawn goes to c4, but it is undefended: the bishop passes b3 and captures it.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.err.c3c4.2: Back to the position: where does the bishop on a2 want to get out? Close that exit.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.fora: That move does not stop Black's plan. Look at the bishop on a2.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.volta: Try again: close the exit of the bishop on a2.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.e1: Attack: now it is your turn to ask. The black bishop is on a2, far from its own pieces. Nobody has a check or a capture that wins material.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.e2: What does Black want? The bishop wants to get out along the diagonal through b3 and come back into play. Your king already covers b1.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.l0: Now the bishop is trapped, and there is no hurry: your king goes after it via b2.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.l1: The black king comes to help, but it is far away.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.l3: The bishop gives itself up for the pawn.
rot.prophylaxis.ideia.bispo.l5: Black wanted to save the bishop along the diagonal. You did not attack it first: you took away its exit, and only then did the king go and get it.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.1: Attacking demonstration: a Lichess game, from a Scotch. The black queen has come into White's camp on c1 and attacks the knight on b1.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.2: Ask what Black wants: the queen wants to get back into play along the diagonal from d2 to g5.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.3: The knight goes to d2 and closes the diagonal. By leaving b1, it opens the first rank, and the rook on a1 now attacks the queen. The queen has no safe square.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.4: The queen captures the rook: it is all she has left.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.5: The white queen recaptures. White gave the rook and won the queen.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra.6: White did not attack the queen first: they closed her exit. Asking what the opponent wanted revealed the move.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.1: Attacking demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in another Lichess game. It is Black's turn, and the white king is on h6, in the corner.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.2: Ask what White wants: the white king can only leave the corner through g5, and from there it goes after your pawns.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.3: The pawn goes to f6 and covers g5: the white king has no way out any more.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.4: White has no other move: the pawn goes to g5 and threatens to capture on f6.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.5: The pawn does not capture: it advances to f5 and keeps the white king trapped. If it captured on g5, the white king would get out through that square.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.regra2.6: The white king has no move, and White can only push the pawn to g6. Black answers with the pawn to f4, and it gets to promotion first. If the h7 pawn captured on g6, the white king would get out through g5.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.1: Attacking demonstration: still with Black, in another Lichess game. Your king is on c5, next to the d4 pawn.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.2: Ask what White wants: the b2 pawn wants to go to b4, give check and drive your king away. The opponent's plan can also be a pawn advance.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.3: The pawn goes to a4. If the b2 pawn goes to b3, the a4 pawn captures it; if it goes to b4, the a4 pawn captures it en passant.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.4: The white king goes to c2: without it, your king would come in through c4 and b3 and capture the b2 pawn.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.5: Your king comes in on c4, and the d4 pawn is free to advance.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.peao.6: Black did not let the b2 pawn advance. With the white king tied to defending that pawn, your king comes into White's camp.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.1: Attacking demonstration: back with White, now the exception. Your king has no escape square: if a black rook reaches the first rank, it may be a back-rank mate.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.2: The prophylactic move would be to open a square for the king with the h2 pawn. But first check the checks, the captures and the threats. The black king has no escape square either.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.3: The queen gives check on d8, defended by the rook on d1.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.4: The black rook captures the queen: it is the only move.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.5: The rook recaptures with mate: the black king has no escape square.
rot.prophylaxis.demos.excecao.6: If White played the pawn to h3, Black would open a square for the king, and the mate would be gone. In a tactical position, the prophylactic move wastes the tempo: check your own checks.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.enuncia: Black wants to bring the g4 knight to e3, against your queen and your rook. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen captured the g4 knight, which was undefended. White is a piece up. With the queen on e2, the prophylaxis, the knight would go back to f6, and the chance would be gone.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.err.d1d: The queen trades queens, but the c6 pawn recaptures, and the g4 knight survives and threatens to come in on e3. Before prophylaxis, check the captures.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.err.d1e: The queen goes to e2 and takes e3 away from the knight, but it goes back to f6, and the piece that was undefended escapes. Before prophylaxis, check the captures.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.err.h2h: The pawn attacks the knight, but it goes to e3, against your queen and the f1 rook. Before prophylaxis, check the captures.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.err.f1e: The rook leaves f1, but the black queen captures your queen on d1, and the g4 knight survives. Before prophylaxis, check the captures.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.valeAqui.err.d1f: The queen goes to f3, but the black queen captures it, and the g4 knight survives. Before prophylaxis, check the captures.
The rook blocks the check, but the black queen captures the a1 rook with check. Get out of check with the king: the f1 rook defends the a1 rook.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.fim: The pawn went to d4 and took e5 away from the black king. When the black pawn went to e5, your pawn went past it to d5, where no black pawn can reach it.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.err.e3d4: The king goes to d4, but the black king drops back to f6, and the black pawn goes to e5 and takes the central squares from your king. Before moving your king, ask where the black king wants to go.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.err.e3d2: The king retreats, and the black pawn goes to e5: the black king comes in through the central squares. Ask where the black king wants to go.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.err.e3e2: The king retreats, and the black pawn goes to e5: the black king comes in through the central squares. Ask where the black king wants to go.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.err.e3f2: The king retreats, and the black pawn goes to e5: the black king comes in through the central squares. Ask where the black king wants to go.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.errPos.d4e5: The pawn captures on e5, but the black king recaptures and reaches the centre. Push the pawn: there is no black pawn in front of it.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.rei.errPos.e3d3: The king retreats, and the black pawn captures on d4. Push the pawn: there is no black pawn in front of it.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.enunciado: Now let us think from Black's side. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.fim: The pawn went to b6 and closed the exit of the a7 bishop. The bishop captured the pawn, and the queen recaptured: Black won the bishop for a pawn.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.err.g7b2: The bishop captures the b2 pawn, but the white rook goes to b1 and attacks it, and Black loses the tempo to close the exit of the a7 bishop. Ask where the white bishop wants to get out.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.err.d5d4: The pawn goes to d4 and closes one exit, but the bishop can still get out through b6. Ask where the white bishop wants to get out.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.err.c7a5: The queen attacks the bishop, but it gets out through d4 and offers the bishop trade. Ask where the white bishop wants to get out.
rot.prophylaxis.pratica.preta.err.c7c2: The queen comes in on c2, but the white rook captures the d5 pawn, and the a7 bishop is still alive. Ask where the white bishop wants to get out.
